info.title: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash Anthropic-Compatible Interface
info.description:
Complete API reference for calling MiniMax-M3.1-Flash via the Anthropic Messages protocol.

**Preview model**: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash is a preview release. Its behavior and parameters may change.

**Compatibility Notes**:
- Path: `/v1/messages` (Anthropic standard path)
- Request / response structure aligns with the Anthropic Messages API
- Supported fields: `model` `messages` (required) `system` `max_tokens` `temperature` `top_p` `stream` `thinking` `output_config` `tools` `tool_choice` `metadata`

**Model Capabilities**:
- Positioning: MiniMax's fast model for day-to-day coding and agent workflows
- Context window: **1,000,000 tokens** (1M)
- Maximum output: **524,288 tokens** (512K), recommended up to **131,072 tokens** (128K)
- Thinking: Always on and cannot be turned off; set the depth with `output_config.effort` (default `max`). Thinking is returned in `content[type=thinking]` blocks
- Multimodal input: Supports text, image, and video content blocks

post.description:
**Preview model**: MiniMax-M3.1-Flash is a preview release. Its behavior and parameters may change.

- Use the Anthropic Messages protocol to call the MiniMax-M3.1-Flash model
- Request / response structure aligns with the Anthropic API
- **Multimodal conversation**: `content` supports text, image, and video content blocks
- **System prompts**: Passed via the top-level `system` field
- **Thinking**: Always on; set the depth with `output_config.effort`. The response `content` starts with `thinking` blocks, followed by `text` / `tool_use` blocks
- **Streaming output**: SSE event stream
- **Tool calling**: Compatible with Anthropic `tool_use` / `tool_result` flow

**Thinking and the output-token limit**:
- Thinking cannot be turned off. Thinking tokens are billed as output tokens, count toward `max_tokens`, and are included in `usage.output_tokens`
- If `max_tokens` is not set, EvoLink uses **32768**
- With a small `max_tokens` and a high effort, thinking can use up the whole limit: the response ends with `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` and no `text` block. Keep `max_tokens` at 32768 or higher, and lower `output_config.effort` for simple tasks
- In multi-turn tool use, send back the assistant's full `content`, including `thinking` blocks, unchanged

**Compatibility rules**:

| Request | EvoLink handling |
| --- | --- |
| `thinking.type: "disabled"` | `thinking` is removed; if `output_config.effort` is not set, it is set to `low` |
| `thinking.type: "enabled"` + `budget_tokens` | Converted to adaptive thinking; if `output_config.effort` is not set, the effort is derived from `budget_tokens`: ≤ 2048 → `low`, ≤ 4096 → `medium`, ≤ 8192 → `high`, ≤ 16384 → `xhigh`, larger → `max` |
| `output_config.effort: "none"` / `"minimal"` | Changed to `low` |
| `service_tier` | Removed; requests always use the standard tier |

Whatever `thinking` or `output_config.effort` value you send, thinking still runs and its tokens are billed as output.

**Ignored parameters**: `top_k`, `stop_sequences`.

model.description:
Model to call

**Note**: `MiniMax-M3.1-Flash` is a preview model, and its behavior may change

max_tokens.description:
Upper limit for generated content length (in tokens), including thinking

**Notes**:
- Maximum **524,288** (512K); recommended up to **131,072** (128K)
- If omitted, EvoLink uses **32768**
- Thinking tokens count toward this limit. With a small value and a high `output_config.effort`, thinking can use up the limit, and the response ends with `stop_reason: "max_tokens"` and no `text` block
- Use 32768 or higher, and lower `output_config.effort` for simple tasks

messages.description:
List of conversation messages, alternating user / assistant turns

**Notes**:
- Must contain at least 1 message
- The last message is typically `role=user`

system.description:
System prompt, used to set the AI's role and behavior

**Notes**:
- Supports a string or an array of strings
- Passed via the top-level `system` field

oneOf.description: System prompt in content block array format. Text blocks may include cache_control

temperature.description:
Sampling temperature

**Notes**:
- Range: `[0, 2]`
- Default 1; higher values produce more divergent output, lower values produce more deterministic output

top_p.description:
Nucleus sampling threshold

**Notes**:
- Range: `[0, 1]`, MiniMax-M3.1-Flash default 0.95
- It is recommended not to adjust temperature and top_p simultaneously

stream.description:
Whether to return via SSE streaming

- `true`: Server-Sent Events streaming response
- `false`: Wait for complete response before returning (default)

thinking.description:
Thinking settings (optional)

MiniMax-M3.1-Flash always thinks, so this field can be omitted. Use `output_config.effort` to set the thinking depth

**Notes**:
- The response `content` starts with `type="thinking"` blocks (billed as output tokens)
- In multi-turn conversations, especially with tool use, send thinking blocks back unchanged

type.description:
- `adaptive`: Thinking on (same as omitting the field)
- `disabled`: Does **not** turn thinking off. EvoLink removes `thinking` and, if `output_config.effort` is not set, sets it to `low`
- `enabled`: Anthropic's legacy style, used with `budget_tokens`. EvoLink converts it to adaptive thinking; if `output_config.effort` is not set, the effort is derived from `budget_tokens`

Thinking runs in every case and is billed as output tokens

budget_tokens.description:
Only used with `type: "enabled"`. It is not a hard thinking limit: if `output_config.effort` is not set, EvoLink converts it into an effort level

- ≤ 2048 → `low`
- ≤ 4096 → `medium`
- ≤ 8192 → `high`
- ≤ 16384 → `xhigh`
- Larger → `max`

output_config.description: Output configuration. Use `effort` to set the thinking depth

effort.description:
Thinking depth

- `low`: Shallowest thinking, fastest response, fewest output tokens
- `medium` / `high` / `xhigh`: Progressively deeper thinking
- `max` (default): Deepest thinking, slowest response, most output tokens

**Notes**:
- Defaults to `max` when omitted; for simple tasks, a lower level reduces latency and output tokens
- Thinking tokens are billed as output tokens and count toward `max_tokens`
- `none` and `minimal` do not turn thinking off: EvoLink changes them to `low`

tools.description:
Tool definition list

**Notes**:
- Follows the Anthropic tool definition specification
- `input_schema` uses a JSON Schema object

tool_choice.description: Tool selection strategy. Only auto and none are supported

type.description:
- `auto`: Model automatically decides whether to call a tool (default when tools are provided)
- `none`: Prohibit tool calls

user_id.description: Unique identifier representing the end user, can be used for per-user monitoring and abuse detection (using a hashed ID is recommended)

role.description:
Message sender role. MiniMax-M3.1-Flash uses alternating user / assistant messages

- `user`: User message (also used to pass back `tool_result` blocks)
- `assistant`: Assistant historical reply (may contain `text` / `thinking` / `tool_use` blocks)

Note: **`system` is not accepted here**: system prompts should be passed via the top-level `system` field.

content.description:
Message content

**Notes**:
- For plain text, pass a string directly
- For structured content, pass a content block array (`text` / `image` / `video` / `tool_use` / `tool_result` / `thinking`)

ContentBlock.description:
Message content block

**Supported types**:
- `text`: Text content
- `image`: Image input
- `video`: Video input
- `tool_use`: Pass back previous assistant tool call
- `tool_result`: Tool execution result
- `thinking`: Pass back previous assistant thinking content
- `mid_conv_system`: Mid-conversation system instruction

source.description: Image or video source, used when type=`image` or type=`video`

input.description: Tool input parameters (JSON object for tool_use)

tool_use_id.description: Corresponding tool call ID (required for tool_result, maps to tool_use.id)

content.description: Tool execution result (tool_result), string or content block array

thinking.description: Assistant thinking content to pass back (used when type=`thinking`). In multi-turn conversations, especially with tool use, pass back the assistant's thinking blocks unchanged

signature.description: Signature for the thinking content being passed back; must be returned as-is for multi-turn continuation

name.description:
Tool name

**Notes**:
- Only `a-zA-Z0-9_-` allowed
- Maximum 64 characters

description.description: Tool description, helps the model determine when to call it

input_schema.description:
JSON Schema object for tool input parameters

**Notes**:
- `type` must be `object`
- Should declare `properties` and `required`

MediaSource.description:
Media source for image or video content blocks

- Images support JPEG / PNG / GIF / WEBP, maximum 10 MB per image
- Videos support MP4 / AVI / MOV / MKV, maximum 50 MB for URL / Base64

media_type.description: Required for base64 input, e.g. `image/png` or `video/mp4`

url.description: Public URL of the image or video

detail.description: Understanding precision, defaults to default. Higher resolution consumes more tokens

fps.description: Video frame extraction rate, default 1, range [0.2, 5]. Higher values are more sensitive to visual changes and consume more tokens

max_long_side_pixel.description: Maximum pixel constraint for the longest side of images or video frames

content.description:
Response content block list

**Possible block types**:
- `thinking`: Reasoning process (always returned for MiniMax-M3.1-Flash, before `text` / `tool_use`)
- `text`: Final answer text
- `tool_use`: Tool call initiated by the model

stop_reason.description:
Stop reason

- `end_turn`: Natural completion
- `max_tokens`: Reached the max_tokens limit (thinking included); if the limit was used up while thinking, there is no `text` block
- `tool_use`: Model triggered a tool call

signature.description: Integrity signature when type=`thinking`, used for multi-turn context verification

input.description: JSON input parameters generated by the model when type=`tool_use`

cache_creation_input_tokens.description: Input tokens used for cache creation

type.description: Error type (e.g. invalid_request_error / authentication_error / billing_error, etc.)

bearerAuth.description:
##All APIs require Bearer Token authentication##

**Get API Key:**

Visit [API Key Management Page](https://evolink.ai/dashboard/keys) to get your API Key

**Add to request header:**
```
Authorization: Bearer YOUR_API_KEY
```

**Note**: EvoLink uses Bearer Token authentication uniformly for `/v1/messages`.
